skills.name: banner-design
skills.title: Banner Design
skills.description: Designs banners for social, ads, website heroes, and print, with multiple art-direction options.
skills.why: Banners and covers are a recurring need for channels and launches.

skills.name: brand
skills.title: Brand
skills.description: Brand voice, visual identity, messaging frameworks, and consistency checks for branded content.
skills.why: Keeps channel and product visuals and tone recognizably on-brand.

skills.name: design
skills.title: Design
skills.description: All-in-one design skill: brand identity, tokens, logos, icons, banners, presentations, and social visuals.
skills.why: Covers the long tail of one-off design asks in a single skill.

skills.name: design-system
skills.title: Design System
skills.description: Design-token architecture (primitive to semantic to component), component specs, and brand-compliant slides.
skills.why: Keeps multi-screen products visually consistent as they grow.

skills.name: slides
skills.title: Slides
skills.description: Creates strategic HTML presentations with charts, design tokens, and responsive layouts.
skills.why: Turns briefs and reports into presentable decks without design software.

skills.name: ui-styling
skills.title: Ui Styling
skills.description: Builds accessible UIs with shadcn/ui, Radix, and Tailwind, plus canvas-based visual designs.
skills.why: The practical implementation partner to the design-system rules.

skills.name: ui-ux-pro-max
skills.title: UI/UX Pro Max
skills.description: Design intelligence for web, mobile, and desktop UIs, with searchable local data on styles, palettes, font pairings, UX guidelines, and stacks.
skills.why: Gives interface work a real design database instead of guesswork; the flagship of the design set.
skills.adaptations: Rewrote ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}-based script paths in SKILL.md to paths relative to the skill folder, so the commands run in any harness.

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.title: Brainstorming
skills.description: Clarifies what the user actually wants, one question at a time, compares 2-3 approaches, and gets a design approved before anything is built.
skills.why: Stops build-first-guess-later work on new features and projects; it is the process that designed this very repo.

skills.name: ponytail
skills.title: Ponytail
skills.description: Lazy senior-dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, explained in one read.
skills.why: Cuts over-engineering, tokens, and cost on everyday coding without dropping safety or tests.

skills.name: ponytail-audit
skills.title: Ponytail Audit
skills.description: One-shot whole-repo audit for bugs, security holes, slow paths, untested risky code, and deletable bloat.
skills.why: A fast health check for inherited or fast-grown codebases, ranked by impact.

skills.name: ponytail-debt
skills.title: Ponytail Debt
skills.description: Lists every deliberate shortcut: marker in the code as a debt ledger.
skills.why: Keeps intentional shortcuts visible so they get repaid instead of forgotten.

skills.name: ponytail-gain
skills.title: Ponytail Gain
skills.description: Shows Ponytail's measured savings in code, cost, and speed from its benchmark.
skills.why: Answers 'is the lazy mode actually paying off' with numbers, not vibes.

skills.name: ponytail-help
skills.title: Ponytail Help
skills.description: Quick reference card for Ponytail levels, skills, and commands.
skills.why: One-shot cheat sheet so the whole set stays usable without re-reading docs.

skills.name: ponytail-review
skills.title: Ponytail Review
skills.description: Quality review of a change: correctness, safety, load behavior, tests, and whether every line earns its place.
skills.why: Catches risky or bloated diffs before they ship, explained in plain language.

skills.name: community-marketing
skills.title: Community Marketing
skills.description: Builds and leverages online communities - Discord, Slack, forums - for product growth and loyalty.
skills.why: Community-led growth fits bot and channel products especially well.

skills.name: competitor-profiling
skills.title: Competitor Profiling
skills.description: Researches competitors from their URLs and produces structured profile dossiers.
skills.why: Know exactly what rivals offer and how they position before you ship.

skills.name: content-strategy
skills.title: Content Strategy
skills.description: Plans what content to create: pillars, topic clusters, editorial calendars, and roadmaps.
skills.why: Deciding what to publish beats publishing at random, for blogs and channels alike.

skills.name: copy-editing
skills.title: Copy Editing
skills.description: Edits and refreshes existing marketing copy: tightening, de-slopping, and sharpening without a rewrite.
skills.why: Most real work is improving copy that already exists, not starting from zero.

skills.name: copywriting
skills.title: Copywriting
skills.description: Writes and improves marketing copy for pages: headlines, CTAs, value propositions, and hero sections.
skills.why: Sharp copy is the cheapest conversion lever for landing pages and product posts.

skills.name: customer-research
skills.title: Customer Research
skills.description: Runs and synthesizes customer research: interviews, surveys, review mining, voice-of-customer, and JTBD.
skills.why: Decisions grounded in real customer language outperform opinion.

skills.name: launch
skills.title: Launch
skills.description: Plans product launches and feature announcements: checklists, go-to-market, waitlists, and release strategy.
skills.why: Launches are one-shot events; a checklist prevents unforced errors.

skills.name: marketing-council
skills.title: Marketing Council
skills.description: Simulates a board of legendary marketers (Godin, Ogilvy, Hormozi, and more) debating your marketing question.
skills.why: Several expert lenses on one decision beat a single generic take.

skills.name: marketing-ideas
skills.title: Marketing Ideas
skills.description: A bank of proven marketing and growth tactics for software products, matched to the situation.
skills.why: The fastest way out of 'we need growth but don't know what to try'.

skills.name: marketing-psychology
skills.title: Marketing Psychology
skills.description: Applies behavioral science and mental models - anchoring, social proof, scarcity, framing - to marketing.
skills.why: Explains why people buy, so offers and copy stop being guesswork.

skills.name: offers
skills.title: Offers
skills.description: Designs the offer itself: value framing, bonus stacks, guarantees, scarcity, and payment structure.
skills.why: A better offer beats better ads; core skill for anything sold or promoted.

skills.name: product-marketing
skills.title: Product Marketing
skills.description: Creates the product-marketing context doc - positioning, audience, ICP, brand voice - that the other marketing skills build on.
skills.why: The foundation of the marketing set: write the context once, reuse it in every campaign.

skills.name: social
skills.title: Social
skills.description: Creates, schedules, and optimizes social media content, and runs social listening across the major platforms.
skills.why: Directly useful for running and growing social and channel presences.

skills.name: video
skills.title: Video
skills.description: Guides AI and programmatic video production: avatars, demos, explainers, and generation pipelines.
skills.why: Video is the highest-reach format; this maps the current tool landscape into workflows.

skills.name: ad-library-teardown
skills.title: Ad Library Teardown
skills.description: Analyzes active ads from Meta, Google, and LinkedIn libraries: hooks, offers, CTAs, and claims.
skills.why: Competitors publish their best-tested messaging in ad libraries for free.

skills.name: audience-research
skills.title: Audience Research
skills.description: Evaluates a creator or brand audience from public signals: demographics, geography, language, and fit.
skills.why: Prevents sponsorship and partnership picks based on follower counts alone.

skills.name: comment-mining
skills.title: Comment Mining
skills.description: Mines comments and replies for objections, questions, buying intent, and voice-of-customer language.
skills.why: Comments are unfiltered market research, already written by the audience.

skills.name: competitor-social-research
skills.title: Competitor Social Research
skills.description: Researches competitors' social strategy and turns public data into a practical strategy brief.
skills.why: Shows what content is winning in your niche and where the gaps are.

skills.name: content-repurposing
skills.title: Content Repurposing
skills.description: Turns public videos, transcripts, and posts into threads, scripts, newsletters, and content calendars.
skills.why: One good source becomes a week of channel-ready material.

skills.name: creator-profile-teardown
skills.title: Creator Profile Teardown
skills.description: Tears down a creator or brand profile: positioning, pillars, hooks, formats, and outlier posts.
skills.why: A repeatable way to learn from accounts that already win.

skills.name: influencer-prospecting
skills.title: Influencer Prospecting
skills.description: Finds and scores creators in a niche for outreach, partnerships, sponsorships, and UGC.
skills.why: Builds prospect lists from evidence instead of manual scrolling.

skills.name: outlier-post-finder
skills.title: Outlier Post Finder
skills.description: Finds posts that massively overperformed a creator's baseline and explains why they worked.
skills.why: Modeling proven outliers is the shortest path to better content.

skills.name: product-demand-research
skills.title: Product Demand Research
skills.description: Validates product ideas by mining pain points, demand signals, and objections from social posts and Reddit.
skills.why: Evidence-backed demand checks before building or launching anything.

skills.name: scrapecreators-api
skills.title: ScrapeCreators API
skills.description: Reference and access layer for the ScrapeCreators REST API: public data from 27+ social platforms.
skills.why: The base skill the whole research set calls; it documents every endpoint the others use.

skills.name: social-listening-brief
skills.title: Social Listening Brief
skills.description: Produces a cited social-listening brief on what people say about a brand, topic, or niche.
skills.why: A fast reputation and sentiment snapshot before campaigns or launches.

skills.name: transcript-intelligence
skills.title: Transcript Intelligence
skills.description: Summarizes and mines video transcripts for hooks, claims, quotes, and reusable content atoms.
skills.why: Unlocks the content inside long videos without watching them all.

skills.name: trend-discovery
skills.title: Trend Discovery
skills.description: Finds trending topics, hashtags, sounds, and formats in a niche from public trend endpoints.
skills.why: Trend timing is free reach for channels; this turns trends into content angles.

skills.name: reverse-engineer-anything
skills.title: Reverse Engineer Anything
skills.description: Reverse engineers binaries, Electron/JS apps, .NET, firmware, and browser targets with REA, backed by runtime evidence.
skills.why: The owner's reverse-engineering workhorse: explains features, compares versions, and guides reconstructions from real artifacts.
